scope: Historical defects and preventive patterns recovered from reviewed work, plus current failures caught by acceptance checks. Each record qualifies its observation and repair evidence; production health requires separate verification.

bugs.title: Stale parent and orphan children consume concurrency
bugs.trigger: A parent attempt dies while durable children retain running state.
bugs.symptom: New work stays capacity-blocked after the real worker is gone.
bugs.rootCause: Occupancy follows raw workflow status rather than canonical live attempts and leases.
bugs.consequence: The scheduler can stop admitting useful work indefinitely.
bugs.repair: Reconcile attempts, leases and effects; recover only proven dead, effect-free targets.
bugs.regressionCheck: Recover orphan children; reject live or effect-ambiguous recovery; verify zero unrelated changes.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Read current occupancy and effect receipts before recovery.

evidence.scope: 9 August reported recovery and natural-cycle checks; not a fresh host observation.

bugs.title: Time-bucket idempotency permits overlapping monitors
bugs.trigger: Equivalent periodic work enters a later time bucket while a prior attempt is live.
bugs.symptom: Two equivalent monitors occupy the same lane.
bugs.rootCause: Time-bucket deduplication lacks a separate live-equivalence admission gate.
bugs.consequence: Duplicate work competes for capacity and may repeat consequences.
bugs.repair: Add single flight keyed by workflow, lane, version and canonical live state.
bugs.regressionCheck: Equivalent concurrent ingress admits once; distinct lane/version admits; later expiry permits admission.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Run bounded concurrent ingress acceptance on the deployed admission path.

evidence.scope: Recovered historical single-flight procedure; no current scheduler mutation executed.

bugs.title: Publication evidence becomes a measured baseline
bugs.trigger: A predecessor has verified publication but no comparable performance snapshot.
bugs.symptom: A challenger is admitted before a measurable baseline exists.
bugs.rootCause: Effect equivalence and measurement maturity are collapsed into one gate.
bugs.consequence: Learning and experiment claims become unsupported.
bugs.repair: Require publication equivalence, comparable measurement and challenger spacing independently.
bugs.regressionCheck: Published but unmeasured predecessor defers; mature comparable evidence permits admission.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Read fresh metrics and test missing versus mature snapshots.

evidence.scope: 13–14 September observations, not current campaign performance.

bugs.title: Unavailable metrics become zero performance
bugs.trigger: Consent, provider availability or low exposure prevents measurement.
bugs.symptom: An agent interprets empty evidence as zero activity.
bugs.rootCause: Missing, blocked, immature and measured-zero states are collapsed.
bugs.consequence: False business conclusions drive unjustified optimisation.
bugs.repair: Preserve explicit unavailable, immature and measured-zero states.
bugs.regressionCheck: Empty connector proves connection only; zero requires an observed measured interval.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Check current unavailable-state rendering and reporting.

evidence.scope: Grounded in recovered empty/unavailable evidence; not a newly reproduced defect.

bugs.title: Guide interaction leaves a partial no-snapshot dashboard
bugs.trigger: A streamed interaction changes dashboard state during snapshot updates.
bugs.symptom: Attention information disappears and sections partly render no-snapshot.
bugs.rootCause: The recovered repair concerns inconsistent snapshot projection; complete current causality is not established.
bugs.consequence: Operators cannot distinguish absent evidence from operational health.
bugs.repair: Keep snapshot semantics and complete rendering consistent across stream transitions.
bugs.regressionCheck: Exercise Guide during updates; verify attention counts, all sections and missing-snapshot semantics.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Reproduce the interaction at the exact deployed console revision.

evidence.scope: Recovered October dashboard repair; not independently repeated live here.

bugs.title: Expanded document JSON exceeds the response budget
bugs.trigger: A large document expands into a verbose serialised tool response.
bugs.symptom: Read fails at the response-size boundary although the document is accessible.
bugs.rootCause: An unnecessarily expanded representation exceeds the response budget.
bugs.consequence: Context recovery stalls or the document is falsely reported missing.
bugs.repair: Use compact native reads or bounded windows with explicit coverage.
bugs.regressionCheck: Read a representative large document compactly and verify intended content and bounds.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Validate the present connector without assuming the old limit is universal.

evidence.scope: Recovered October read recovery; limits depend on tool and representation.

bugs.title: First client theme differs from server HTML
bugs.trigger: A dark-theme route hydrates server light-theme markup.
bugs.symptom: React reports a hydration mismatch or replaces content.
bugs.rootCause: Provider initial state differs between server and first client render; delays do not fix the contract.
bugs.consequence: Rendering is unreliable and suppressed warnings conceal the cause.
bugs.repair: Match server and first-client theme state; apply browser preferences after hydration.
bugs.regressionCheck: Check light/dark mobile and desktop first renders and unexpected mismatch warnings.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Run deployed-route hydration checks across supported browser conditions.

evidence.scope: Application-specific repair and reported browser checks; other providers need separate acceptance.

bugs.title: App metadata substitutes for customer permission
bugs.trigger: Installation-token metadata decides customer write admission.
bugs.symptom: Valid work is rejected or App capability stands in for customer writer authority.
bugs.rootCause: Installation capability and authenticated customer permission are treated as one principal.
bugs.consequence: Objective admission is incorrect or exceeds customer authority.
bugs.repair: Check identity-bound customer permission separately from selected App capability.
bugs.regressionCheck: Test reader/writer customers, unselected repositories and missing App permissions independently.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Complete a fresh permitted customer journey.

evidence.scope: Merged/deployed repair recorded; current customer role is read and no fresh write objective established.

bugs.title: Admitted writes recreate state after account deletion
bugs.trigger: A request admitted before deletion completes after cleanup.
bugs.rootCause: Session rejection does not fence already-admitted durable writes.
bugs.repair: Fence stale writes at registry and credential destinations using deletion/generation state.
bugs.regressionCheck: Pause admitted work, erase, resume, and verify no indexed state or credential resurrection.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Revalidate indexed destinations and each actual deletion; track external revocation separately.

evidence.scope: Synthetic write-race acceptance is separate from real account cleanup and external revocation.

bugs.title: Duplicate-payment early return loses outcome evidence
bugs.trigger: Fulfilment succeeds, evidence fails, then the valid event is redelivered.
bugs.symptom: A duplicate is acknowledged without repairing the missing outcome.
bugs.rootCause: Fulfilment idempotency short-circuits independently incomplete evidence.
bugs.consequence: Successful paid work remains absent from the outcome ledger.
bugs.repair: Reconcile evidence independently of already-completed fulfilment.
bugs.regressionCheck: Fail evidence once, replay, and verify one fulfilment plus one recovered durable outcome.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Inject controlled evidence failure and read unchanged customer effect counts.

evidence.scope: Source contains reconciliation; complete production fault injection remains separate.

bugs.title: Cursor advances before uncorrelated evidence is durable
bugs.trigger: An outcome precedes publication evidence and holding persistence fails or fills.
bugs.symptom: The source event can be skipped after cursor acknowledgement.
bugs.repair: Persist validated holding before advancing the cursor; retain progress on failure.
bugs.regressionCheck: Inject full storage and persistence failure; verify cursor remains before the event, then recover fairly.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Run current crash, capacity and restart acceptance with cursor readback.

evidence.scope: Implementation protects this failure mode; not every production crash path was exercised.

bugs.title: Payment signature becomes campaign provenance
bugs.trigger: A valid payment contains caller-supplied campaign labels.
bugs.symptom: Unsigned labels enter attribution as authenticated source identity.
bugs.rootCause: Payment authenticity is incorrectly extended to unsigned provenance fields.
bugs.consequence: Spoofed attribution corrupts business reporting and learning.
bugs.repair: Validate signed or source-owned attribution separately from payment evidence.
bugs.regressionCheck: Valid payment with unsigned labels stays paid but unattributed; trusted provenance can correlate independently.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Check forged, absent and valid attribution at the deployed boundary.

evidence.scope: Signed attribution is present; descriptive correlation does not establish causation.

bugs.title: Omitted services produce schema-valid numeric filler
bugs.trigger: A minimal brief omits services or supplies an empty list.
bugs.symptom: The handoff passes schema with meaningless numeric service filler.
bugs.rootCause: Optional-input fallback preserves shape without useful output semantics.
bugs.consequence: A successful response cannot support the intended website handoff.
bugs.repair: Handle omitted and empty inputs deliberately; assert meaningful output content.
bugs.regressionCheck: Check both omitted and empty services through the real public journey.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Recheck merge/deployment and run fresh omitted/empty-input customer acceptance.

evidence.scope: PR 8 open at reviewed head dd72e2d; patch is not deployment or clean-account acceptance.

bugs.title: External readers claim a closed-world boundary
bugs.trigger: A tool reads GitHub entities while claiming closed-world annotations.
bugs.rootCause: Read-only is confused with no external-world interaction.
bugs.consequence: Provider activation and agent interpretation rely on inaccurate metadata.
bugs.repair: Annotate external readers accurately and retain compatibility checks for local validators.
bugs.regressionCheck: Inspect actual tools/list; separate external readers and local validators; retain version checks.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Verify production discovery, conversational routing and settled publication separately.

evidence.scope: Recorded merge/deployment and scans; provider publication and clean-account acceptance remain separate.

bugs.title: Analytics helper mismatches SQL and sampling semantics
bugs.trigger: Telemetry is queried through legacy Workers Analytics Engine SQL.
bugs.symptom: Request/parsing errors or unweighted aggregates misstate outcomes.
bugs.rootCause: Request format, response parsing and explicit legacy sample weighting are mismatched.
bugs.consequence: Transport success or volume becomes a false usage or demand claim.
bugs.repair: Use actual raw-SQL and response contracts, weighting and transport/tool outcome separation.
bugs.regressionCheck: Validate real response, weighted aggregates and HTTP-success/tool-failure separation.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Revalidate endpoint semantics and report sampling and identity limits.

evidence.scope: Helper repair established; historical telemetry includes owner/test traffic without user/cause markers.

bugs.title: Runbook warnings and dashboard fields drift
bugs.trigger: Docs, warnings and projections are maintained independently.
bugs.symptom: Unknown evidence appears healthy or automatic work appears manual.
bugs.rootCause: Units, ownership and recovery semantics lack a shared executable contract.
bugs.consequence: Operators take incorrect actions or accept unsupported health.
bugs.repair: Generate references/examples from versioned canonical field and warning contracts.
bugs.regressionCheck: Check warning semantics, units, missing values and projection parity against fixtures.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Check deployed UI, generated docs and contract version together.

evidence.scope: Contracts and saved acceptance reviewed; console fixture speed is not provider throughput.

bugs.title: Stale provider list contradicts settled submission detail
bugs.trigger: The list still says not submitted after submission of the same draft.
bugs.symptom: List and settled detail disagree about in-review state.
bugs.rootCause: State propagation is a candidate explanation; provider internals were not established.
bugs.consequence: An agent may retry an already completed consequential action.
bugs.repair: Read same-draft settled detail and action receipt before deciding on a retry.
bugs.regressionCheck: Stale list plus settled in-review detail must trigger readback rather than duplicate submission.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Retain exact draft/action locators and verify settled state before retry.

evidence.scope: Settled detail resolved the conflict; no duplicate retry occurred and root cause is unproven.

bugs.title: Agent declares completion from a lower evidence layer
bugs.trigger: The highest result is a test, HTTP success, owner demo or merge.
bugs.symptom: Agent reports deployed or customer-complete without matching evidence.
bugs.rootCause: Implementation, transport, release, publication and customer outcome become one done state.
bugs.consequence: Later work resumes from an unsupported assumption.
bugs.repair: Record highest evidenced transition with revision, environment, principal and limits.
bugs.regressionCheck: Merged without deployment stays merged; owner success without fresh customer journey stays owner-scoped.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Collect the missing deployment, provider or customer evidence for the claimed outcome.

evidence.scope: Cross-project continuation pattern; not a newly reproduced defect or proof every agent made the error.

bugs.title: Unsupported API write falls through to HTML success
bugs.trigger: An agent sends POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE to a GET-only discovery endpoint.
bugs.symptom: The framework returns HTML with HTTP 200 instead of rejecting the unsupported method.
bugs.rootCause: A missing method handler falls through to the application renderer; declaring GET alone does not enforce HTTP method rejection.
bugs.consequence: Agent clients can mistake a successful HTTP response for an accepted write or handoff.
bugs.repair: Declare explicit write-method handlers returning 405 with Allow: GET on each read-only JSON route.
bugs.regressionCheck: Check POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE against registry, integration brief and coding bug JSON: all twelve pairs must return 405 and Allow: GET.
bugs.nextAcceptance: Verify method rejection on the exact deployed origin after release.

evidence.scope: CI run 37901366579 observed POST returning 200. The repair then passed all twelve method/surface checks on the local Node preview on 9 October. Production deployment remains unverified.
